findings.description: The async `retry_any.__ror__` checks `isinstance(other, retry_all)` when it should check `retry_any`, and the async `retry_all.__rand__` checks `retry_all` correctly. The `__ror__` check is therefore wrong: it unpacks a `retry_all`'s retries into a `retry_any`.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `sync_retry_all | async_retry_any`. `retry_base.__or__` dispatches to `other.__ror__(self)`, and the `isinstance(other, retry_all)` branch fires. The result is `retry_any(*all.retries, *any.retries)`, which turns an AND group into separate OR members. The `retry_all` semantics are silently lost, so retries happen under the wrong conditions.
